cause: The DM described Bede's exam from the paralysis alone and forgot the 6 damage it had just narrated and wrote in its own notes (5 HP of 11).

The player's wish to spend the silver on Piper was played as Garn pocketing the purse again, undoing a gift the DM had narrated and counted on the sheet line; the sheet was never changed and the notebook never recorded the purse.

Not a real clash: on Day 3 Brannoc left five of his ten candles on the step and kept five, so five at the lamp-house and five in the pack can both be true; only the phrase 'your five candles' was loose.

The DM restated the chapel's place from memory as two hours and a mile past the ford instead of the notebook's 'just past a ford', an hour from Greywater, and the chapel entry was not in the shown notes.

Asked whether Brannoc still carried Hob's message, the DM said it was all delivered on Day 4 and invented that the later 'lamp was lit' word was passed on, though that word was given on Day 7 and the notebook never recorded it.
The DM made up a backstory (turned back at a flood, trying to get home) that contradicts its own notebook (she set out for Stonebridge) and the fact she walked up the causeway away from Reedholm.
In R128 the DM hinted village fires would help without checking the wisp's stats; in R129, after looking at the rules, it said fire and spears are useless, so the earlier hint was an unchecked guess.

The notebook correctly had Wren from Greywater (north), but the summary was broken and the notebook entry was not in the shown notes, so Pim's line made up 'from the south' (the DM later wrote it off as Pim being careless).

One reply earlier Wren said she stopped the game a year ago and they had gone back to it; the DM then invented, in the rhyme note and reply, that Fen started it last month, and the 'stopped a year ago' fact was never written to the notebook.

The Black Ford was placed differently each time: the notebook said half a day from Reedholm on the causeway, the Tamsin crossing in R143 put it right across the channel from the village, and R152/R153 said a mile, then twenty minutes (with an invented 'village crept toward it' note).

Wren's line (six and a half hours) and the DM's own count (eight and three-quarter hours) sit in the same reply; the 8:45 sum is right and Wren's figure was a slip, likely confusing dawn at 6:30 with a number of hours.

Loose narration: the lights have hung there a while in the story, but 'all week' is said about Tamsin's own watching when she only arrived the evening before; nothing in the notebook fixes how long the lights have shown.

The notebook and R156 had the Isle about forty paces long, but the DM gave the walk round it as a quarter hour and charged 12 minutes, so it did not work out the travel time from the size it had just given.
The DM invented that the stone's lamp, reed and wave match the marks on the post, though its own R152 text had only a reed or a wave under each name; the detail was not in the notebook.

The player had the same rope tied round a stone as a lifeline and then asked to tie the bundle with it; the DM went along without noting the rope had to be untied, so this is mostly a player-driven slip.
The DM narrated the horn as one short blast in R174 and then had Ode say it went twice in R176; the number was not written anywhere to check against.
